text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-api.us-west1.p99 > 1.2s for last 6m. Related: node reports ECC and thermal events. Paging infra-oncall. Incident created (INC-2026-0314-17).

maria: paging @sam and @henry — can you grab triage? seeing streaming stalls and tail latency spike.

sam: on it. pulling logs now. quick summary from metrics: p95 still ~180ms, p99 jumped from ~800ms -> ~2.1s. error-rate normal, but streaming stalls correlate with specific accelerator nodes.

henry: digging into traces — stalls start when token index ~512+ and KV cache hits drop. Looks like long-running token adds are queueing on some worker processes.

maria: which nodes? preliminary filter: us-west1-accel-pool-3 node-57, node-59 showing thermal/ECC alerts. grabbing node logs.

sam: paste of dmesg from node-57: 
```
[ 4621.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=12345, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 4621.123459] nvidia: GPU-0: GPU reported ECC error, corrected (type: single-bit)
[ 4621.123460] thermal 0000:65:00: critical temp reached: 92C
```

maria: thanks. also see repeated ECC corrected counts in monitoring for GPU-0 over last 45m. ops-bot, did auto-eviction trigger?

ops-bot: auto-eviction policy: ECC corrected threshold=10/hour, current count=7 in last 60m — no auto-evict yet.

sam: ok, mitigation plan: 1) cordon+drain node-57, 2) route streaming traffic away from pool-3 via routing policy to us-west1-fallback (quantized-L2) for a temporary period, 3) spin up replacement warm instance.

henry: also reduce max_batch_size on the streaming scheduler for us-west1 to limit tail amplification while we rebuild. recommend from 32 -> 16.

maria: executing drain now: `kubectl cordon node-57 && kubectl drain node-57 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

sam: pods evicted, drain progress 90% — one long-lived pod still terminating (stream session). forcing graceful-termination timeout to 15s to avoid stuck sessions: `kubectl patch pod <pod> -p '{"spec":{"terminationGracePeriodSeconds":15}}'`

maria: drain complete. node-57 cordoned. routing policy updated: added temporary override to route new streaming sessions to quantized-L2 in us-west1 and to fallback replicas in region-eu if capacity needed.

henry: made scheduler change: max_batch_size=16, scheduler-queue=200. Observability: p99 dropped from 2.1s -> 860ms in 8m after routing + batch change. p95 stable.

tessa: CS update: saw about ~120 streaming sessions with hiccups in the 21:00–21:10 window; top affected customers are flagged and ticket opened (CS-7891). No evidence of data loss. Customers experiencing partial stalls and some reconnects.

sam: hardware note: iLO logs show repeated thermal trip events for node-57 and nearby node-59. suspect rack-level cooling issue + marginal GPU thermal interface. filing hardware ticket with DC ops.

maria: for the immediate customer impact assessment: we estimate ~2% of total streaming requests saw >1s latency, ~0.3% timed out (client-side). SLO: p99 target for streaming = 500ms, so still impacted but trending better.

ops-bot: enrichment: matching instances in the pool with ECC counts >5 in last 2h: [node-57, node-59, node-64]. Recommended manual inspection.

henry: agreed follow-ups: automatic evict rule: ECC corrected > 3 within 1h -> evict node. Lowering threshold to avoid these tail events. Also add thermal trip as immediate eviction.

sam: ordering replacement GPU for node-57, scheduling onsite tech to inspect heatsink / airflow. For now node-57 will remain cordoned/offline.

maria: quick live mitigation checklist I've executed: 
- cordoned/drained node-57
- routing override to quantized-L2 and added fallback replicas
- decreased batch size and scheduler queue
- notified CS & created customer tickets

henry: follow-ups to capture in postmortem: 
- firmware update on GPUs where ECC corrected trending up
- add automated routing circuit-breaker: if region p99 > 700ms for >5m then failover to fallback variant
- improve observability: emit per-accelerator ECC-rate alert with auto-evict suggestion

tessa: I'll coordinate customer comms draft once we have final numbers. keep me posted if we need to escalate to enterprise SLAs.

sam: monitoring shows p99 now ~520ms and still dropping. will keep routing override for another 30m and then gradually shift traffic back while we observe.

maria: creating incident ticket and assigning postmortem to eng-runtime + infra. initial impact summary will be sent to leadership and shared channels.

oncall-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: node-57 cordoned/drained at 1807776780; routing override applied at 1807776795; scheduler updated at 1807776810.

sam: closing live mitigation — node offline for replacement; warm replacements in service. continuing to monitor until p99 below 500ms for 20m.

henry: notes for postmortem: replicate ECC conditions in test lab if possible, add thermal probe alerts at rack level, consider policy to reduce GPU duty-cycle when corrected-ECC-rate rises.

maria: thanks team. will file postmortem with timeline, impact numbers, and remediation items. tagging follow-ups: infra (sam), runtime (henry), cs (tessa).

ops-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. will auto-close if p99 < 500ms for 30m.

tessa: copying customers list into CS ticket and scheduling outreach for tomorrow morning.

maria: final note: please upload any logs or screenshots to the incident ticket. I"ll add RN about changed thresholds and automation. :white_check_mark:
